title: In the Rijksmuseum print cabinets
summary: With more than 750,000 prints and drawings, the Rijksmuseum's collection is one of the largest in the world. Because of the fragility of the material, we rotate the selection in the print cabinets every six month, allowing us to share new stories each time. This presentation focuses on Roman street art, social satire and Japanese fairy tales. There is also a cabinet dedicated to the Van Eeghen Drawing Book, a unique 17th-century drawing book recently gifted to the museum.

title: Willem de Kooning at work
summary: One hundred years ago, Willem de Kooning left the Netherlands for a new life in New York, where he became one of the most influential artists of the 20th century. This autumn, he returns, with a major retrospective of his drawings, complemented by a selection of celebrated paintings and sculptures. Alongside the exhibition, two of his most iconic paintings will be displayed in the Gallery of Honour. This exhibition is made possible through the generous support of The Willem de Kooning Foundation, The Friends Lottery, Ammodo Art, Art Mentor Foundation Lucerne, Blockbusterfonds, Rijksmuseum International Circle, Rijksmuseum Friends and the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science.

title: Document Netherlands: New Energy
summary: Kadir van Lohuizen photographs the energy transition on and around the North Sea From offshore wind farms in the open sea to heavily secured data centers, the energy transition is taking place on a scale that is almost impossible to comprehend, largely beyond our view. Photographer and filmmaker Kadir van Lohuizen shows how the North Sea and the surrounding countries are changing at a breakneck speed due to the rising demand for energy. The exhibition is made possible in part by Floor Fonds/Rijksmuseum Fonds and Rijksmuseum NEXT.

title: Drawing!

A group of artist friends, including Hendrick Goltzius, Jacques de Gheyn II, and Abraham Bloemaert, found each other in their drive for innovation. Together they brought the art of drawing to unprecedented heights.

title: Ed van der Elsken: Up Close
summary: A cyclist cheekily sticking out her tongue, tough youths on Amsterdam's Nieuwendijk, young women in miniskirts. From The Netherlands to Cuba and Japan, Ed van der Elsken chased the same unfiltered energy. Different streets, a different time - and yet you recognise it. From his first steps as a photojournalist to the design of his final photo book With handwritten notes, contact prints, experiments from the darkroom Who was the man behind the camera? A journey through his work and life

title: Fake!

title: REVOLUSI!
summary: Diplomats, freedom fighters, victims, liberators. Everyone has a different view.
